# Deferred-Anchor Registry — Production

> The canonical source of truth for every `D-*` anchor cited in `src/` but
> deferred to a future cycle. The leading underscore sorts this file before
> the numbered plans in directory listings — call this out as the registry,
> not a plan. Per-plan §3.1 rows are still the preferred home for anchors
> whose feature area maps cleanly onto a plan; this file catches the orphans
> + cross-cutting anchors that don't belong to any single plan.

> **CI/pre-commit guard** (`scripts/check-anchor-registry/check-anchor-registry.{sh,ps1}`): every
> `D-*` identifier appearing in `src/` MUST resolve to a row in ANY of the three
> registry documents (a closed anchor's row lives in `-done.md`, and a citation of
> it must still resolve)
> OR a citation in any `.plans/*.md`. Pre-fix this recurred TWICE
> (memory: "the same gap silent-failure caught for MULTI-PAGE-GOT").
> The guard makes the system enforce the discipline — same shape as the
> agnosticism veto + the `CallConv` static_assert.
>
> **★ ANCHOR-NAME RULE — READ BEFORE INVENTING A `D-*` NAME (documented 2026-07-28, TF-C81; it was
> load-bearing and unwritten until it bit).** The guard's regex is
> `D-[A-Z0-9_]+(-[A-Z0-9_]+){2,}` — **`D-` plus THREE OR MORE `-`-separated segments is a
> DEFERRED-WORK ANCHOR and MUST resolve to a row here; a TWO-segment `D-*` name (`D-OPT`) is an
> informal feature label the guard ignores.** So hyphenating a COMPOUND FEATURE WORD silently changes
> the identifier's CLASS: `D-CSUBSET-ALWAYS-INLINE` tripped the guard and had to be renamed
> `D-CSUBSET-ALWAYSINLINE` to match its sibling `D-CSUBSET-NOINLINE`. The failure surfaces as
> “missing row”, which misdirects you into WRITING a duplicate row instead of FIXING the name.
> **Spell a compound feature word as ONE segment (`ALWAYSINLINE`, `NOINLINE`); reserve hyphens for
> genuine name components; when in doubt, match the sibling anchor already in this file.** Full
> write-up: [[D-PLANS-ANCHOR-NAME-SEGMENT-COUNT-GATE]].

> **★★ MEASUREMENT CAVEAT — READ BEFORE QUOTING ANY “this will clear N errors” NUMBER IN THIS FILE (2026-07-28, macOS-arm64 predefine-probe cycle).** DSS **abandons a TU at its first hard parse failure**, so a corpus error count is a count of the errors REACHED, never of the defects PRESENT. Clearing an early blocker therefore EXPOSES later ones that were never reached, and a drop in the total is NOT a count of defects fixed. Worked example from this cycle: the 189-TU sqlite build went **213 → 80** total errors when architecture + toolchain predefines were both supplied — that is **NOT 133 defects fixed**; the residual 80 is a NEWLY-EXPOSED population whose composition was unknown until separately measured. It is equally possible for a real fix to make the total go UP (this cycle measured exactly that: toolchain-identity macros ALONE took 213 → 216). Every forward estimate of the form “closing X clears N errors” in any row below MUST be read with this caveat, and every new one MUST carry it. See [[D-MEASURE-FIRST-FAILURE-MASKS-RESIDUAL]] for the citable class row.

> `_deferred-anchor-registry-{harness|production}.md` is a list of remaining items, that
> always delete a done item and put into `_deferred-anchor-registry-done.md` once

> ⚠ **THE AUDIT TRAIL IS NOT DELETED, IT IS RELOCATED.** The preamble above still

> ⚠ **A CLOSED ROW IN THIS FILE IS A REFUSAL**, not untidiness:
> `check-anchor-balance` fails the tree for it. Close a row with
> `scripts/apply-registry-row/apply-registry-row.py`, which performs the move itself --
> hand-editing the table is how the two halves drift.
>
> **THE LINE BETWEEN PRODUCTION AND HARNESS, so a borderline row is decided by a rule and
> not by taste:**
> **PRODUCTION** is a defect a USER OF THE COMPILER could hit -- it is in the shipped binary
> or in the config that binary reads (front end, preprocessor, semantics, HIR/MIR/LIR,
> optimiser, assembler, linker, object formats, FFI surface, diagnostics, CLI, emitted
> runtime).
> **HARNESS** is a defect only WE can hit -- tests, gates, guards, the cycle machinery,
> plans, scripts, carriages, CI, the example corpus AS a corpus.
> ⚠ `D-CONFIG-*` and `D-DIAG-*` are PRODUCTION deliberately: a `.lang/.target/.format.json`
> document IS the compiler's behaviour in this architecture, and a diagnostic is its output to a
> user. Filing either as tooling would hide real conformance defects in the harness pile, which is
> the exact thing that split exists to stop.
> ⚠ A row's bucket follows the DEFECT, never the instrument that found it: a corpus example that
> reveals a codegen bug files under codegen.
>
> ★ **RESOLUTION READS ALL THREE FILES; ORIENTATION READS ONLY THE TWO WORKING ONES.**
> A `D-*` cited in `src/` must resolve wherever its row now lives, so every guard that
> RESOLVES a citation globs `_deferred-anchor-registry*.md`. Every instrument that asks
> *what is left* -- `burndown-queue`, the cycle's priority pick -- reads production and
> harness ONLY. Reading the archive to choose work is how a closed row got recommended
> three times in this project's history.

## Anchor Index

**Row shape: EXACTLY six cells — `Anchor`, `Priority`, `Status`, `Trigger`, `Closing work`, `Cross-refs`.**
★★★ **`Priority` IS `P0`..`P5` AND `Status` IS ONE OF `✅ CLOSED` / `🟠 OPEN` / `⏳ GATED` / `🔵 DISCLOSED` — a controlled vocabulary, added
2026-09-01 on the operator's instruction: *"add columns for priority and status ... this way
we always have clean statuses."* Before that the verdict was the FIRST GLYPH of a prose blob
that also carried the trigger, the history and the retraction, and every reader had to agree
where the verdict stopped — which is precisely the agreement that failed four times in
`check-anchor-balance`'s own comment history.
⚠ **THE STATUS CELL KEEPS ITS GLYPH, AND THE GLYPH IS THE CONTRACT.** A row is CLOSED iff its
status cell OPENS with ✅ after stripping `*_ ` — the complement defined, never the variants,
so a glyph nobody has thought of yet counts OPEN. A column holding the bare WORD `CLOSED`
would make that test false for every closed row at once.
ⓘ **The cells are what `dssharness` writes and reads:** `✅ CLOSED`, `🟠 OPEN`, `⏳ GATED`, `🔵 DISCLOSED`; a
`--status-file` holds one of them (or the bare word `closed`/`open`/`gated`/`disclosed`). The older spelling
`🔵 🟠 OPEN (DISCLOSED)` is REFUSED by the tool (✔MEASURED 2026-09-23: four rows written in it were refused
before any was applied); it survives only as history in the handoff.
★★★ **`🔵 DISCLOSED` IS OPEN WORK WHOSE DEBT PRE-DATES THIS CYCLE, AND IT EXISTS TO
REMOVE AN INCENTIVE RATHER THAN TO GRANT AN EXCUSE.** The balance gate forbids a cycle that
OPENS new debt; it does not forbid one that DISCLOSES pre-existing debt. Those are different
quantities — and while the writer could not spell the second, the cheapest way to pass the gate
was to not write the row at all: the precise dishonesty the gate exists to prevent, produced BY
the gate. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-16 at `91820d36`, which is worse than "no new row could carry it":
the six-cell migration moved every surviving disclosure claim into the `Trigger` cell while
`is_disclosed` reads `Status`, so **the exemption was reaching ZERO rows in either registry**.
A disclosed row counts in every total, files in a WORKING registry, and `--done` refuses it; it
is exempt from the net-increase FAILURE and from nothing else whatsoever.
⚠ **The claim is CHECKABLE, which is why it is a word and not a flag.** It asserts the defect
PRE-DATES this cycle, so a reviewer can look for it in the base ref. Marking a defect this cycle
introduced is a false statement about history, not a formatting choice. The word is for the reader.
⚠ **`Priority` IS A DECLARATION, NOT A SIEVE RESULT.** `burndown-queue` seeds it and then
READS it; its own docstring warns that a band is *"a sort key, not a verdict"* because a
census built from that keyword sieve reported 103 where the truth was 4. Correct the cell and
the correction survives, which re-running a sieve never does.
★ **DO NOT HAND-WRITE A ROW.** `scripts/anchors/anchors.py` (and its `write-anchor` /
`set-anchor` / `read-anchor` / `read-anchors` launchers) takes the FIELDS and produces the row,
so a wrapped id, an unescaped pipe and a wrong cell count are all inexpressible.
A row with fewer cells shifts every following cell one column LEFT; a row with more
has the surplus SILENTLY DROPPED by the renderer. Neither is visible when reading the
raw text, so the count is load-bearing — see `D-PLANS-REGISTRY-MALFORMED-ROW-CELLS`.

Two authoring rules follow from that, both verified against the GitHub renderer:
- **A raw `|` splits a cell EVEN INSIDE BACKTICKS.** To quote an expression, regex or
  alternation containing one, write `\|` — the backslash-escaped form is the *only*
  one that survives inside a code span (an HTML entity does **not**).
- **` ═══ ` inside a cell marks a seam where two cells were joined** when a row
  authored to a wider schema was converged onto these four columns. It is a joint in
  the prose, not a column boundary.

⚠ **APPEND AT END-OF-TABLE, NEVER AT END-OF-FILE.** This registry once carried a
second `## Anchor Index (continued)` table, which existed only because rows had been
appended past the Allowlist over many cycles; its header declared TWO columns, so every
fuller row silently lost its `Closing work` and `Cross-refs`. The 2026-08-25
production/harness split merged both tables, so each file now has exactly ONE index and
the accident cannot recur here -- but the rule that prevents it still has to be obeyed.

| `D-PP-DATETIME-BUF-SIZED-FOR-VALID-TM-ONLY` | P2 | 🟠 OPEN | 🟢 **FIX LANDED 2026-08-03 — VERIFICATION PENDING on the host that surfaced it. ★ THE FIRST FINDING PRODUCED BY THE NATIVE arm64 HOST, AND IT IS A FINDING ABOUT THE HOST AS AN INSTRUMENT AS MUCH AS ABOUT THE CODE.** ✔MEASURED: building DSS with gcc-13 Release on real aarch64 hardware (Ubuntu 24.04, the Oracle VPS commissioned 2026-08-03) emits `-Wformat-truncation` at `src/analysis/preprocess/preprocessor.cpp:4530` — *"`__builtin___snprintf_chk` output 9 or more bytes (assuming 19) into a destination of size 16"* — for the `__DATE__` spelling in `MacroExpander::computeDateTime`. **The x86_64 legs (Windows MSVC/Ninja-g++, WSL gcc, clang-19) do NOT report it**, so three green legs and a 777-test suite were silent about it; the diagnosis is that aarch64 gcc inlines `computeDateTime` far enough up the `preprocess()` chain to see the bound, and the x86_64 legs do not. ⚠ **BE PRECISE ABOUT SEVERITY — the loose reading of this is wrong.** It is **NOT** a memory-safety bug and **NOT** an overflow: `snprintf` bounds its own write, so the only reachable harm is a TRUNCATED, i.e. WRONG, `__DATE__` string. It is also **not reachable from a sane clock** — `"Mmm dd yyyy"` is 11 chars + NUL and fits `char buf[16]` for every well-formed `tm`. **ROOT CAUSE is an INCONSISTENT DEFENSIVE POSTURE, and that is the real defect:** the function already range-checks `tm_mon` into `[0,12)` before indexing `kMon` — so its author was explicitly contemplating a malformed `tm` — yet passes `tm_mday` and `tm_year + 1900` straight through to `%2d`/`%04d`, where an out-of-range `int` needs up to 11 chars each and the format's true worst case is 3 + 1 + 11 + 1 + 11 + NUL = **28 bytes into a 16-byte buffer**. Guarding one field of a struct and not its siblings is the shape that rots. | **FIX (landed):** size both buffers for the format's WORST CASE over arbitrary `int` rather than for a well-formed date — `buf[32]` for `__DATE__` (28 needed) and `buf[40]` for `__TIME__` (three `%02d` at <=11 + two colons + NUL = 36) — so truncation is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE instead of merely improbable. ⓘ **Chosen over clamping `tm_mday`/`tm_year` deliberately:** a clamp silently substitutes a wrong-but-plausible date and depends on the clamp staying correct, whereas correct sizing cannot be defeated by any input and needs no future maintenance; the `tm_mon` clamp stays because it guards an ARRAY INDEX, which sizing cannot help. ⚠ **REMAINING WORK — do not stamp this CLOSED until both are done: (1)** rebuild on the aarch64 host and confirm the warning is GONE (the fix was authored on an x86_64 host that never reproduced the warning, so it is currently UNVERIFIED against the only instrument that shows it — asserting otherwise would be exactly the error this registry exists to prevent); **(2)** decide whether the aarch64 leg should build `-Werror`, since a warning that only ONE host emits and no gate fails on is a warning nobody will read — that is the generalisable half, and it is worth more than this one buffer. | ✔MEASURED 2026-08-03 on the native arm64 VPS (aarch64 Ubuntu 24.04.4, gcc-13.3.0, Release) during the first native build of this project; warning text quoted verbatim above. ✔TREE `src/analysis/preprocess/preprocessor.cpp` (`MacroExpander::computeDateTime`). ★ **THE REUSABLE LESSON, which outlives the buffer:** a NEW HOST IS A NEW INSTRUMENT, and its first run is worth reading for what it says about the other legs — this warning had been latent through every green gate the project has ever run, and it took ninety minutes of arm64 hardware to surface. Expect more of these as the host is used; each is evidence about x86_64 coverage, not merely about arm64. · Sibling class an instrument that does not state its scope reports a scoped result as an unscoped claim (a green whose scope was narrower than it read) · every host builds every target, proven artefact by artefact rather than by dispatch arm (the any-host requirement this host was commissioned to serve). |

Required so OPT7's §2.9 inline-legality gates have a real source (not only hand-built MIR). **DESIGN-LOCKED 2026-06-04 (cycle 12, user GO = "most complete"):** scope = `static`→`Local` + C-faithful `__attribute__((weak))`→`Weak` + `__attribute__((visibility("default"\ — "hidden"\ | "protected")))`→`Visibility`. **Architecture**: (1) grammar — add `StaticKeyword`+`AttributeKeyword` + an optional specifier prefix on `topLevelDecl`, **[SUPERSEDED by the as-built design — see `D-DECL-SPECIFIER-PREFIX-SUBSTRATE` row below; reconciled per cycle-13 audit §I]**: the original framing "modeled as MARKERS (NOT positional children), like `constMarker`/`variadicMarker`, so `name:1/type:0` stay stable" was WRONG — a `constMarker` rides INSIDE the type subtree (`subtreeContainsToken`), but `static`/`__attribute__` is a genuine LEADING SIBLING, so it cannot be a type-nested marker. Cycle 12 built the real resolution: an OPTIONAL positional prefix child + a resolver that STRIPS it (`specifierPrefixRule` + `declRoleChildren`/`descendVisibleDecl`/`findInitExprInDecl`) before resolving the positional `name:1/type:0` indices — the indices stay stable WITH the strip, not by pretending the prefix isn't a positional child; (2) NEW agnostic `linkageSpecifiers` facet in the `.lang.json` `semantics` block mapping c-subset specifiers → the universal `SymbolBinding`/`SymbolVisibility` vocab (engine learns ZERO C-specific facts; unknown-key fail-loud); (3) HIR linkage attribute reusing `core/types/symbol_attrs.hpp` enums (NOT `FfiLinkage` — it lacks `Local`); (4) CstToHir populates it from markers + facet; (5) `hir_to_mir` maps → MIR binding (closes sibling `D-OPT7-LINKAGE-HIR-TO-MIR-MAPPING` same cycle). Tests: MIR-tier per-form (strict) + single-CU `static`→DCE pin + parse + agnosticism. `weak` runtime behavior stays deferred to OPT7+cross-CU (`D-OPT7-WEAK-INLINE-NEGATIVE-PIN`); P1 lands the full source→MIR path + MIR-tier proof. architecture confirmed + index-wrinkle resolved this invocation. **AUDIT GO (dss-audit design-review 2026-06-04)** — premises verified vs code (symbol_attrs reuse; FfiLinkage lacks Local; P2 stub = `hir_to_mir.cpp`; DCE + rebuilder already preserve binding + consult `isExternallyVisible`; `builtinTypes` is the agnosticism precedent). **Build is held to 4 closure gates**: (1) lowering is a GENERIC facet lookup via `symbolBindingFromName` — NO `if(spec=="static")` hardcode anywhere in CstToHir/hir_to_mir; agnosticism scan stays clean (the #1 audit check); (2) the `static`→`Local` DCE pin must be RED-ON-DISABLE — a `Local` fn + an identical `Global` twin, both genuinely unreferenced, binding the SOLE driver of eliminated-vs-kept (cycle-11 vacuity discipline) + strict per-form `ASSERT_EQ(binding/visibility)`; (3) unknown facet key → config-load reject; unknown source `__attribute__((x))` → **fail-loud error + diagnostic** (fork SETTLED: error, not warn-and-ignore — aligns §A.4 + auditor lean; silent-ignore off the table); (4) OPT7 boundary NOT crossed (no inlining / cross-CU; weak runtime stays pinned to `D-OPT7-WEAK-INLINE-NEGATIVE-PIN`). **Watch-item**: confirm `attributeSpecifier` (double-paren + string-literal arg) is pure-config-expressible (no parser/engine change); if it needs engine work, surface it as a separate substrate surface — don't absorb silently. **SUBSTRATE LANDED (cycle 12)** — `D-DECL-SPECIFIER-PREFIX-SUBSTRATE` ✅ CLOSED; P1 is now buildable. Next cycle wires c-subset `static`/`__attribute__` (grammar + `linkageSpecifiers` facet + HIR linkage attribute + `hir_to_mir` mapping + the `static`→DCE pin). | **Pre-OPT7 step P1 — BINDING SPECIFIERS LANDED cycle 13; visibility-syntax deferred; unknown-specifier-diagnostic ✅ CLOSED cycle 14 (registry). Priority: high (pre-OPT7).** · migrated from `.plans/22-optimizer-plan - tbd.md` |

| `D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL-INITIAL-EXEC` | P3 | 🟠 OPEN | 🟠 **P3 GENUINELY UNDONE — ROW WRITTEN 2026-09-16 (cycle P68, lane `cit`) FOR AN ID CITED 3 TIMES IN PRODUCTION CODE, AND NAMED IN SEVERAL SIBLING ROWS' PROSE, WITH NO ROW OF ITS OWN.** **WHAT IS MISSING:** the initial-exec TLS model — a loader-filled `tpoff` GOT slot — which is the only way to bind a TRUE LIBRARY thread-local, i.e. an `extern thread_local` whose definition no sibling CU supplies (the glibc `errno` class). **NO SHIPPED BINDING MODEL CAN CARRY ONE, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE CORRECT ANSWER RATHER THAN A GAP:** got-indirect binds ONE process-shared address per object, which is the antithesis of thread storage — every thread would alias one datum — so reaching for it would be a silent mis-bind, not a degradation. The linker therefore fail-louds with `K_FormatLacksThreadLocalSupport`, naming this anchor and telling the user the one thing that DOES work today: an intra-program `extern thread_local` resolves when its defining translation unit is compiled into the same program, because the definition's own `MirGlobal.isThreadLocal` drives the layout and the import is folded away like any extern data. The hypothesis is dead and the slowdown is a property of that host or of what the tests now ask of it. ⚠⚠ **IT ALREADY COSTS A GATE RUN, NOT JUST TIME.** The first run FAILED `analysis/compilation_unit/test_import_resolver_shuffled` on a **ctest TIMEOUT**, not an assertion. That test took **315.02 s** against a 315 s budget in run 1 and **14.37 s** in run 2 — a 22x swing on identical code, while the leg TOTAL barely moved, so the swing is the test's own and not the host's load. A budget that one host sits on the edge of turns every future round into a coin flip. ⓘ WHERE THE TIME GOES, macOS run 2 against the same names on Windows Debug in the same round: `analysis/preprocess/test_preprocessor_shuffled` 1305 s vs 238 s, `analysis/semantic/test_fc3_width_semantics_shuffled` 948 s vs 131 s, `analysis/semantic/test_semantic_analyzer_c_shuffled` 618 s vs 99 s, plus `program/test_emit_hir_round_trips_every_example` at 997 s and `hir/test_frontend_deep_nesting_costs_heap` at 678 s. Five of the six run in about 2.5 s on macOS DEBUG with this same tree, and under a second on MSVC Release. ✔**IT DID NOT REPRODUCE**: the re-taken leg was **2170 / 2170 green in 842 s**, against 1170 s for the red one. So this is evidence about RELIABILITY, not about a hang, and the row must not be read as naming a defect in the tested code. ⇒ **The two sides together are the actual finding: the leg's cost has grown until an ordinary transient turns a BUDGET red.** ⓘ A third incident in the same round, same host, different layer: WSL's mDNS missed the Mac **twelve times running** while Windows resolved it and found port 22 OPEN — the resolver, not the host. WHAT THE EDITOR DOES TODAY (`src/lsp/workspace_project.cpp` `selectDocumentConfigurations`): a LISTED document is analyzed under exactly the manifests whose expanded `sources` contain it (`core::PathIdentity` membership), under each of their pairs, with each manifest's `includes` and `defines`; an UNLISTED document gets every manifest of its language, and any diagnostic not every configuration reports is tagged `[target=<spec>, …]`. The direction is CONSERVATIVE: the includers' own configurations are always among those checked, so nothing the build would report is hidden — the cost is a tagged false alarm from a manifest that never compiles the header, and only when one workspace root holds two or more manifests of one language with DIFFERENT configurations. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-21: every one of the 9 tracked manifests is alone in its directory, and none of the repo's six multi-target workspaces holds a header at all, so no in-tree workspace reaches the over-check today. THE DESIGN THAT FITS: an INCREMENTAL per-source include index — each listed source's include closure per configuration, RECORDED as the preprocessor opens files (not re-derived from rendered buffers, which drop a header that contributed no text), built once in the background and refreshed per CHANGED file (a changed source re-preprocesses that source alone; a changed header re-preprocesses only the sources whose recorded closure holds it; a manifest change re-plans its own sources) — never a full preprocess per refresh. An unlisted file is then checked under the configurations whose index holds it, and one no index holds (no includer at all) keeps the tagged all-manifests rule. ⚠ BOUNDARY: nested (`dependsOn`) manifests are not read by the editor at all, so a header a DEPENDENCY's sources include is checked under the root's configurations only — a separate, wider question. Trigger: the first workspace — in-tree or reported — whose root holds two manifests of one language with different configurations and a header that only some of them include. P1, SILENT: DSS'S ADDRESS OF A LIBRARY FUNCTION IS THE IMAGE'S OWN STUB, NOT THE FUNCTION'S ADDRESS, SO IT COMPARES UNEQUAL TO THAT FUNCTION'S ADDRESS EVERYWHERE ELSE IN THE PROCESS.** ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23 on WSL x86_64 (gcc 13 with GNU ld 2.42, clang 18 with ld.lld 18.1.3, DSS ELF x86_64 exec), each probe comparing an address with `dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "puts")`, where 42 means equal: C `(void *)&puts` gives gcc -no-pie 42, gcc -pie 42, clang -no-pie 42, clang -pie 42, DSS 1. C `static int (*p)(const char *) = puts;` gives the same four 42s, DSS 1. A `.s` `.quad puts` gives the four references 42, DSS 1. A `.s` `leaq puts(%rip)` is where the references FORK: GNU ld -no-pie points a PC32 in code at a PLT entry it does not make canonical (1, dynsym `puts` st_value 0), lld makes the entry canonical (42), gcc -pie refuses the PC32, and DSS gives 1. The mechanism (✔MEASURED, objdump of the DSS images): C `&puts` lowers to `lea puts@plt(%rip)`, the stub the format's call dispatch provides; the dynsym `puts` is NOTYPE UND with value 0 and its slot is GLOB_DAT, so the loader binds the slot to the library's `puts`, and nothing binds any other reference to the stub. C23 6.5.9 makes two pointers to the same function compare equal, and POSIX `dlsym` returns that function's address, so a program that compares `&puts` with a pointer a library hands back gets the wrong answer where every reference gets the right one. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23 on PE, against `GetProcAddress` on ucrtbase.dll or msvcrt.dll: MSVC 19.51 cl /O2 /MD gives 42, because the ucrt header declares `puts` dllimport and `&puts` is the IAT value; mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 gives 1, because its header declares no dllimport and `&puts` is the `jmp *__imp_puts` thunk (read with objdump); DSS gives 1, for C and for a `.s` `.quad puts`. So on PE the references split by the header's declaration, and MSVC, the platform vendor, agrees with C23. INFERRED, not measured: the aarch64 ELF arms take the same stub; Mach-O is not measured. | Every reference must say whether it CALLS the function or TAKES ITS ADDRESS. Today the x86_64 C-codegen `lea` variants declare the call kind `rel32` for a data reference (the data-reference relocation kind, lane `xa`'s tranche item 4). Then, ruled 2026-09-23 by the coordinator, the FORMAT config decides between two answers, never a format name in core code: (1) an executable makes the stub CANONICAL: dynsym `st_value` = the stub's address, STT_FUNC, with the image's own slot bound through a PLT-class relocation (`R_X86_64_JUMP_SLOT` / `R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT`), which the loader resolves past an undefined-with-value definition, so the slot cannot bind to its own stub. This is lld's answer, and GNU ld's whenever a reference needs pointer equality. (2) A PIE or a shared object, which cannot carry a canonical stub, LOADS the address from the slot (the -fPIE answer), and a static initializer gets a dynamic relocation at its own slot. PE follows MSVC: the address is the IAT value. Pins: `&puts`, the static initializer and `.quad puts` compared with `dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "puts")` on exec and PIE, x86_64 and aarch64 under qemu, each 42; the PE twin against `GetProcAddress`; a CALL control that still goes through the stub; a red-on-disable that puts the stub back. | [[D-ASM-ADDRESS-OPERAND-CANNOT-NAME-AN-UNDEFINED-SYMBOL]] (its `.s` address of a library function takes the same stub) · [[D-LK6-11]] (lazy binding: the PLT-class relocation) · `appendDynsymEntry` (`src/link/format/elf.cpp`) · lane `xa` findings m9 and m11 |

P1, A VALID PROGRAM OF ONE REFERENCE REFUSED: MSVC's sized integer suffixes. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-24, MSVC 19.51 (`/std:c17`, `/W4`): `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64` and their unsigned forms `ui8` … `ui64`, the `i` and the `u` each in either case (24 spellings), compile without a diagnostic, run, and work in `#if`. Their meaning is not 6.4.4.1's ladder: the suffix FIXES the type — `i8` plain `char`, `ui8` `unsigned char`, `i16` `short`, `ui16` `unsigned short`, `i32` `int`, `ui32` `unsigned int`, `i64` `long long`, `ui64` `unsigned long long` — and a magnitude past that type's range is reduced modulo 2^N with no warning (`300i8` is `char` 44, `4294967296i32` is `int` 0, `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFi64` is `long long` −1). gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 (`-std=c11 -pedantic-errors` and gcc's default mode) and mingw-w64 gcc refuse all 24; DSS refuses them with P_MalformedNumber (`5i64`, `5ui64`, `5i32`, measured on x86_64 PE). Under `DSS = (gcc ∪ clang ∪ MSVC) ∪ ISO C` one accepting reference makes a spelling required, and MSVC is the only witness of its meaning. Windows code writes them (`0xFFFFFFFFui64`, `1i64 << 40`), and MSVC's own `<limits.h>` spells `LLONG_MAX` as `9223372036854775807i64`. Not a list edit like the mixed-case spellings: the C language document's `integerLiteralTyping` rules are first-fitting-candidate ladders whose last miss is S_IntegerLiteralTooLarge, and these need a rule with ONE fixed type whose out-of-range magnitude wraps — a rule shape the loader and the three literal typers (the semantic tier, `cst_const_eval`, and phase 4's `pp_if_eval`) do not have. | Declare the sized suffixes in the C language document as integer-literal rules of a new, closed shape — the suffix spellings, ONE type named through the same type resolution as the ladder's candidates, and the out-of-range behaviour as a declared verb (`wrap`, MSVC's measured one) — with the lexer list extended to match and the loader's cover-exactly-once cross-check spanning both rule shapes. The literal typers read the rule, never the spelling: the semantic tier, `cst_const_eval` and phase 4 (`pp_if_eval`, where the value takes the phase-4 width after the wrap). Pins: every one of the 24 spellings typed and valued as MSVC does at a small value and at each range edge (`127i8`/`128i8`, `0xFFi8`, `256ui8`, `2147483648i32`, `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFi64`), in `#if` too; the loader refusing a sized rule without a type or with an unknown out-of-range verb; a runnable example with a `release` arm that MSVC runs to 42 and gcc/clang refuse; red-on-disable dropping one spelling and changing the verb. | `src/dss-config/sources/c.lang.json` (`numberStyle.integerSuffixes`, `semantics.integerLiteralTyping`) · `src/core/types/grammar_schema_json.cpp` (the `integerLiteralTyping` loader and its cross-checks) · `src/core/types/integer_literal_ladder.hpp` · `src/hir/cst_const_eval.cpp` · `src/analysis/preprocess/pp_if_eval.cpp` · [[D-C-MIXED-CASE-INTEGER-SUFFIXES-REFUSED]] (the measurement that found it) |

No program is known to miscompile: diagnostic-level, not ABI. The folding rule is exact for all five (C 6.3.1.4 / 6.3.1.5 fix the result of converting a representable constant), so the fold must compute the same correctly rounded or truncated value the hardware would — never a host-`double` shortcut for an F32 or a u64 that `double` cannot hold. | Teach the release pipeline's constant folder the five floating conversions of a constant operand — SIToFP, UIToFP, FPToSI, FPToUI, FPExt/FPTrunc — each computing exactly the value the target's hardware conversion produces: correctly rounded to the destination format (to nearest, ties to even, one rounding, never a host `double` shortcut for an F32 or for a u64 that `double` cannot hold), truncated toward zero for float to integer, and NOT folded where C leaves the result undefined (an out-of-range float to integer), so the fold never invents a value the unoptimized program would not compute.
